sections.h2: Where is Bartlett, and why does the county matter?
sections.html:
Bartlett is a Chicago-area village split mostly between Cook and DuPage counties, with a small parcel at its western edge in Kane County. The 2020 census counted 41,105 residents, and the July 2025 Census estimate of 40,855 is 0.7% below the 2020 base.

Three counties mean three recorders and three tax offices. The first move in any Bartlett sale is reading the parcel number on your tax bill to learn which one applies.

sections.h2: How did Bartlett get its name and its housing stock?
sections.html:
The village is named for Luther Bartlett, who in 1873 gave money and half of his 40-acre woodlot to help build a railroad depot. A petition for incorporation went to Springfield on February 11, 1891, and the village was incorporated on June 21, 1892. The original 1873 station still stands as the Bartlett Depot Museum.

Most of the population growth came in the 1980s, so the village's growth is recent compared with the depot-era town center. The 2020 census listed 14,522 housing units, of which 2.2% were vacant, and a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9%.

sections.h2: What is the Bartlett community like for buyers?
sections.html:
Bartlett skews toward owner-occupied family housing. About 89% of homes are owner-occupied, the average household has 2.85 people, and the 2020 census found that 36.6% of households had children under 18. The median household income in 2020-2024 was $133,240.

  • Asian residents make up 19.7% of the population and Hispanic or Latino residents 15.0%, according to the Census Bureau.
  • 22.4% of residents are foreign-born.
  • The mean commute to work is 29.7 minutes.
  • Two-thirds of 2020 households were married-couple households.

The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, which opened on August 8, 2004 on Illinois Route 59 just south of U.S. Route 20, draws visitors from across the region. Villa Olivia, a year-round resort with a golf course and winter sports, dates to 1926.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads serve Bartlett homes?
sections.html:
Public schools in Bartlett are entirely within Elgin Area School District U46, the second largest district in Illinois. Bartlett High School, Eastview Middle School and elementary schools named Bartlett, Centennial, Sycamore Trails, Prairieview, Nature Ridge and Liberty serve the village, and some students attend South Elgin High School or Kenyon Woods Middle School in South Elgin.

Illinois Route 59 is the main north-south road, with a large retail area at Route 59 and Stearns Road. The Milwaukee District West rail line stops at Bartlett station and runs east to Chicago Union Station, and Pace bus Route 554 connects the village to Elgin and Schaumburg. Buyers who commute by rail will ask how far a house is from the platform.

sections.h2: What should a Bartlett seller know about permits?
sections.html:
The village's Building Division issues permits for work from decks and pools to driveways and new construction, and inspections by building staff run Monday through Friday only. You can reach the division at 630.540.5920.

The village's guidance on new driveways is specific and worth reading before you list a house with a worn drive.

  • The apron, the part of the driveway that meets the street, is the homeowner's responsibility, and the village does not maintain or replace it.
  • Public works inspects the public sidewalk and utilities inside the driveway during permit review, and if the sidewalk needs repair the village will do it, which can take up to four weeks and delay the permit.
  • No apron extension is approved when a parkway tree stands within 10 feet of it, and the village will not remove parkway trees for that purpose.
  • If a concrete contractor repairs the public sidewalk, Public Works will reimburse part of the cost, and the number to ask is 630-837-0811.

Sprinklers and invisible fences placed in the village right-of-way are also the homeowner's problem if sidewalk work damages them.

sections.h2: What does the economy around Bartlett look like?
sections.html:
Apart from the downtown, Bartlett's retail is concentrated at Illinois Route 59 and Stearns Road. Census figures for 2022 show $196.5 million in retail sales, or $4,897 per resident, along with $117.7 million in health care receipts and $89.3 million in transportation and warehousing receipts.

About 71.7% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and 49.5% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Persons in poverty stand at 4.2%, and 97.1% of households have a computer. Mean travel time to work is 29.7 minutes, so buyers weigh Route 59 access and the rail line.

sections.h2: What do parks, the library and village government offer residents?
sections.html:
Bartlett has a village president, six trustees and a village clerk, all elected at large on a nonpartisan ballot to four-year terms, with municipal elections held in odd-numbered years. The Bartlett Park District runs the Bartlett Community Center at 700 S. Bartlett Road, which hosts youth and adult sports, swimming and an open gym.

The Bartlett Public Library opened in 1973 and was renovated in 2015 with new study rooms, conference rooms and an art room. The village has a large Little League program, including a Challenger division for players with special needs, and holds an Independence Day festival near the community center and an arts fair on the last weekend of June.

These facts help when you write a listing or talk to a buyer, since families often ask about recreation within a few minutes of the house.

sections.h2: How do the deed, transfer declaration and recording work in Bartlett?
sections.html:
County recorders sell the revenue stamps that pay Illinois' transfer tax, according to the Department of Revenue. Home rule municipalities may add their own tax, so ask the title company whether the village charges one.

The PTAX-203 declaration goes to the county of the parcel. In Cook County the Clerk's deed fee is $107 on the schedule that began April 1, 2024, a sum covering recording, GIS, storage, the state rental housing support fee and a filer fee. Parcels in DuPage or Kane have their own fee lists, so call that recorder.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale worth considering in Bartlett?
sections.html:
A tidy house can go through a regular listing. A cash offer suits a house needing major work, a move on a deadline, or an estate.

  • Get the offer in writing and see who pays closing costs.
  • Name the title company early and learn which recorder will file the deed.
  • Hold on to the recorded deed and your copy of the transfer declaration.

faqs.q: Which county holds my Bartlett parcel?
faqs.a: Read the parcel number on your tax bill. Bartlett is mostly in Cook and DuPage counties, plus a small piece of Kane. That county's recorder files the deed and its treasurer collects the tax.

faqs.q: What does a deed filing cost at the Cook County Clerk?
faqs.a: $107 on the schedule effective April 1, 2024. It rolls together the county recording fee, a GIS fee, a storage fee, the state rental housing support fee and a non-government filer fee. DuPage and Kane parcels follow those counties' fees.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for a new driveway?
faqs.a: Yes. The Building Division issues driveway permits, and public works reviews the sidewalk and utilities inside the driveway. Any sidewalk repair can take up to four weeks and hold up the permit, so apply early and call 630.540.5920.

faqs.q: Who runs the schools in Bartlett?
faqs.a: Elgin Area School District U46, the second largest in Illinois, serves the entire village. Some residents' children go to South Elgin High School instead of Bartlett High School.

faqs.q: May I sell in as-is condition?
faqs.a: Yes, either to a cash buyer or through a listing priced for the condition. Pull your permit record first so nothing surprises the buyer.
